role: The aggregator serving this Control Panel — the API every surface on this host talks to.
readOnlyReason: The Control Panel API publishes its own configuration for reading only. Applying a change means restarting it, which would kill the request asking for the change and take the panel down with it — so its settings are edited in /etc/kgsm-api/kgsm-api.env and applied by restarting the service.

fields.label: Log level
fields.description: Minimum severity this API logs.

fields.label: Listen address
fields.description: Addresses this API serves on. The Control Panel and every other surface reach it here.

fields.label: Allowed browser origins
fields.description: Exact origins a browser may call this API from. A panel served from an origin that is not listed is refused by the browser before the request arrives.

fields.label: Host id
fields.description: Identity this host is known by across the whole ecosystem — the audience its tokens are minted for, and the key its stored metrics and history hang off. Empty uses the machine name.

fields.label: Display name
fields.description: Friendly name shown for this host in the panel. Empty falls back to the host id.

fields.label: Region
fields.description: Where this host is, shown alongside it in a multi-host view. Free text, purely descriptive.

fields.label: Cluster node id
fields.description: Identity this host uses inside a cluster. Empty uses the host id.

fields.label: Public base URL
fields.description: Externally reachable address of this panel, used where a link has to work from outside the host. Empty means links are built from the incoming request instead.

fields.label: Monitor socket
fields.description: The metrics daemon's socket. Wrong and the metrics capability reports unavailable rather than guessing at numbers.

fields.label: Watchdog socket
fields.description: The supervisor's control socket, which every start and stop of a native server goes through.

fields.label: Assistant URL
fields.description: Where the assistant serves. Empty means this host has no assistant and the chat surface reports it absent.

fields.label: Assistant relay secret
fields.description: Shared secret letting this API ask the assistant on a signed-in user's behalf. It has to match the assistant's own relay secret.

fields.label: Firewall socket
fields.description: The firewall authority's socket. Empty means port state is reported as unknown rather than assumed closed.

fields.label: Scheduler socket
fields.description: The scheduler's status socket. Empty means the next scheduled restart shows as unknown.

fields.label: KGSM executable
fields.description: Path to the KGSM executable. Everything this API knows about servers, blueprints and configuration is read through it.

fields.label: KGSM event journal
fields.description: Directory holding the engine's append-only event journal, which the API reads to see what the engine did. Read-only and shared with every other consumer — nothing needs configuring on the engine side.

fields.label: systemctl path
fields.description: Which systemctl to run when reading a leaf's state or restarting it.

fields.label: journalctl path
fields.description: Which journalctl to run when reading a leaf's logs.

fields.label: Server list refresh
fields.description: How often the list of servers and their run state is re-read from the engine.

fields.label: Metrics refresh
fields.description: How often metrics are scraped from the monitor and pushed to connected panels.

fields.label: Services refresh
fields.description: How often each leaf's systemd state and health are re-read for the Services board.

fields.label: Update check interval
fields.description: How often each server is checked for an available update.

fields.label: Backup scan interval
fields.description: How often each server's backups are re-scanned for the panel's backup KPIs. A backup taken or restored through KGSM refreshes that server immediately, so this only bounds how quickly other changes are noticed.

fields.label: Disable update checks
fields.description: Stops checking whether servers have updates available. The panel then shows no update state at all rather than a stale one.

fields.label: Server detail cache
fields.description: How long a server's detail is reused before being re-read from the engine.

fields.label: Blueprint cache
fields.description: How long the blueprint catalog is reused before being re-read from the engine.

fields.label: Disable resource alerts
fields.description: Stops raising alerts when host or server resource use crosses a threshold.

fields.label: Disable authentication
fields.description: Turns off every authentication check and treats each caller as an administrator. Intended for local development only — on a reachable host it hands full control of every server to anyone who can connect.

fields.label: Token signing key
fields.description: Secret every session token is signed with. Changing it signs everyone out at once, which is also how you revoke every token in a hurry.

fields.label: Discord application id
fields.description: The Discord application users sign in through.

fields.label: Discord client secret
fields.description: Secret for that application, used to complete a sign-in server-side.

fields.label: Discord bot token
fields.description: Token for the same application, used to read whether someone is in the server and which roles they hold.

fields.label: Discord server id
fields.description: The Discord server whose membership decides who may sign in. Everyone in it can at least look; roles decide the rest.

fields.label: Sign-in redirect
fields.description: Where Discord sends someone back to after they approve. It has to match the redirect registered on the Discord application exactly.

fields.label: Panel URL
fields.description: Where to send someone once sign-in completes. Empty returns them to where they started.

fields.label: Administrator roles
fields.description: Discord roles granted full control, including configuring leaves and connecting hosts.

fields.label: Operator roles
fields.description: Discord roles allowed to run and change servers, but not to administer the host itself.

fields.label: Viewer roles
fields.description: Discord roles allowed to look but not act. Anyone in the server can already look, so this is only worth setting to name it explicitly.

fields.label: Disable the session registry
fields.description: Stops tracking live sessions. Signing in still works, but a token can no longer be revoked before it expires and the Active Sessions list goes empty.

fields.label: Session lookup cache
fields.description: How long a session's validity is reused before it is checked again. Longer means fewer lookups and a longer wait before a revoked session actually stops working.

fields.label: Expired session cleanup
fields.description: How often expired sessions are cleared out of the registry.

fields.label: Maximum session age
fields.description: How long a session can keep renewing itself before the user has to sign in again, however active they are.

fields.label: RAWG API key
fields.description: Key for the game-metadata service used for descriptions and artwork. Empty means the panel shows what the blueprints carry and nothing more.

fields.label: Artwork cache directory
fields.description: Where downloaded artwork is kept. Pointing it elsewhere abandons what is already downloaded and fetches everything again.

fields.label: Steam art base URL
fields.description: Where Steam cover art is fetched from.

fields.label: Disable Steam cover art
fields.description: Stops using Steam for cover art, leaving the metadata service as the only source.

fields.label: Library refresh interval
fields.description: How often the game library's metadata and artwork are refreshed. Zero turns the scheduled refresh off.

fields.label: Library refresh hour
fields.description: Hour of the day the refresh runs, in this host's local time.

fields.label: Directory listing limit
fields.description: How many entries one directory listing returns before it is cut short.

fields.label: Editable file size limit
fields.description: How large a server file may be and still be opened in the editor.

fields.label: Editable blueprint size limit
fields.description: How large a blueprint may be and still be opened in the editor.

fields.label: Log sources
fields.description: Which journal units the host's Logs tab reads. Empty uses the known leaf units.

fields.label: Log read timeout
fields.description: How long to wait for the journal before giving up on a log request.

fields.label: Override directory
fields.description: Where this API writes each leaf's configuration override. It has to match what the leaves' drop-ins load, or every change is written and never read.

fields.label: Descriptor directory
fields.description: Where leaves publish what they can be configured with. Pointing it elsewhere leaves every leaf's configuration page empty.

fields.label: Drop-in directory
fields.description: Where the per-leaf systemd drop-ins live. It is how this API tells whether a change can actually be delivered to a leaf.

fields.label: Post-change health window
fields.description: How long a leaf is watched after a configuration change before the change is rolled back as unhealthy.

fields.label: Cluster secret
fields.description: Shared secret every host in the cluster authenticates to the others with. Empty means this host is standalone.

fields.label: Previous cluster secret
fields.description: The secret being rotated away from, still accepted so the cluster does not split apart mid-rotation.

fields.label: Advertised URL
fields.description: Address other hosts should reach this one at. Empty means this host does not advertise itself.

fields.label: Peer URL
fields.description: A peer to learn the rest of the cluster from. Empty means this host waits to be contacted.

fields.label: Peer exchange interval
fields.description: How often this host exchanges what it knows with a peer.

fields.label: Peer refresh interval
fields.description: How often each peer's state is re-read.

fields.label: Peer suspect timeout
fields.description: How long a silent peer is tolerated before it is treated as suspect.

fields.label: Peer removal timeout
fields.description: How long a suspect peer is kept before it is dropped from the cluster.

fields.label: Outbox drain interval
fields.description: How often queued messages for other hosts are sent.

fields.label: Cluster cleanup interval
fields.description: How often delivered and expired cluster messages are cleared out.

fields.label: Undelivered message lifetime
fields.description: How long a message for an unreachable host keeps being retried before it is given up on.

fields.label: Cluster message retention
fields.description: How long delivered cluster messages are kept before being deleted. Must outlast the retry window, or a message could be deleted while still being retried.

fields.label: Database file
fields.description: File holding this API's own records — the audit trail, live sessions, and per-host settings. Pointing it elsewhere starts empty and leaves the existing history behind.
